contracts.claim: Atomic publication and pointer persistence use real PostgreSQL semantics.
Projection lifecycle state and persistence remain internally consistent.
Batch provider and computation call counts remain bounded for a representative universe.
Review runtime blocker states close truthfully against PostgreSQL.
AfterClose crash, restart, fencing, checkpoint, and resume semantics do not false-green or duplicate downstream work.
Canonical Review observations round-trip and remain idempotent in PostgreSQL.
Concurrent history progress writers preserve updates and checkpoint visibility.
History v3 projection materializes idempotently through the production PostgreSQL persistence contract.
Review current facts bind to the selected same-day Core run and fail closed without legacy fallback.
DSA compatibility projection and publication remain an explicit, independently persisted consumer.
Review HTTP routing, authorization, lineage, errors, and client-facing fields use the production app contract.
Serial and bounded-spawn Bars scheduler paths persist equivalent daily and minute facts idempotently.
Review scope history/cross-sectional are built from the formal published-Review date axis (reuse of FORMAL REVIEW READ OWNER), preserve missing-date slots as null, and exclude broken-pointer dates.

Price Composition history (capital_tilt + leadership) is read only from the formally published run of each date; an unpublished same-day run cannot pollute it, and a published date without that scope's Composition keeps a null date slot.

Explorer compare-first read (ReviewScopeObservationFact LEFT JOIN ReviewScopeCompositionSnapshot) takes compareFacts only from the formally published run; an unpublished same-day run cannot pollute facts or the Composition LEFT JOIN. When industry_l1 and concept coexist, peer percentile is computed per family, never cross-family.

For users resolved from explicit user_capabilities (legacy_plan_fallback / C10 excluded), self_selection, market_data, and research_replay are enforced independently at the market-data boundary. scope=market requires market_data. scope=watchlist requires self_selection and is constrained server-side to the current user's active UserWatchlistItem membership. Instrument-scope stock-detail endpoints, including bars, quote, chart-snapshot, indicators, structural-factors, temporal-features, instruments/{id}/events, and instruments/{id}/send-feishu, allow market_data for any instrument or self_selection only for an instrument in that user's active watchlist. Symbol-scope stock-detail endpoints stocks/{symbol}/context and stocks/{symbol}/first-pyramid use the same resource-scope authorization through require_stock_symbol_market_access. export authorization uses body.scope as the single source of truth. No capability is inherited; research_replay-only is denied. Anonymous access is 401, market_data-only access to scope=watchlist is 403, research_replay-only access to market data and stock detail is 403, and a market_data user passes the guard before business validation (invalid timeframe -> 400 / nonexistent instrument -> 404).

For users resolved from explicit user_capabilities (legacy_plan_fallback / C10 excluded from this contract), /v1/watchlist/monitor-status requires self_selection only and exposes only that user's own active watchlist (200 for self_selection-only and both, 403 for market_data-only, 200 for admin); GET /v1/watchlist requires self_selection only (403 for market_data-only); POST and DELETE /v1/watchlist require self_selection only (403 for market_data-only). GET /v1/watchlist returns metadata-only summary items (watchlist_item_id/instrument_id/symbol/name/market/source/created_at) and never exposes market/strategy metrics (price, change_pct, metrics, latest_event, BB, node, POC, first_pyramid, bars).
